messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 Pager — routing/fallback: detected unexpected spillover of hosted traffic into Dedicated pool 'dedicated-west'. High error rate (504/429) and increased latency for tenants on that pool. Paging on-call.
kevin: Oncall here — seeing a spike, attaching quick metrics. Hosted spike started ~1846805000, errorrate in dedicated-west from 0.2% -> 9%.
anna: I can confirm. Traces show many requests from hosted-tenant matcher with policy 'spillover: enabled' hitting dedicated-west. Looks like tenant isolation match rule mis-evaluated, mapping hosted-route -> dedicated pool for a subset of requests.
jordan: Adding: we just rolled routing policy set 'tierBlend: preferred:dedi, fallback:hosted' in last deploy (1846799000). Need to check config semantics — maybe priority inversion for region fallback.
sre-lead: Triage plan: 1) pause spillover routing policy, 2) pin affected tenants off dedicated-west, 3) scale up temporary capacity if needed. Kevin take lead on mitigation, Anna on forensics.
kevin: Doing step 1 now — running command:

```
redwoodctl routing update --policy-id=rt-3471 --set spillover=false --reason="emergency stop spillover" 
```

will update live policy, should stop new hosted->dedicated matches.
anna: While that's running, I'm pulling sample requests to verify which tenant id's were misrouted.
kevin: Policy updated (ok). Observability: new hosted traffic to dedicated-west dropped to near-zero after 24s. Errorrate on dedicated-west decreasing but there are queued KV-cache issues causing a small tail of 5xxs.
infra-ops: Re: KV cache — evicting stale cache for dedicated-west pools now:

```
redwoodctl pool evict --pool dedicated-west --scope=tenant --filter=spillover
```

infra-ops: Evict done.
jordan: Root cause hypothesis: A recent matcher change to region_fallback logic let 'hosted' routes match the 'dedicated' selector when region fallback kicked in for west->west-eu pairing. Essentially, modelVariant and tenant_isolation rule order was wrong.
liaison-cs: Do we have an impact list? Which customer tenants hit 429/504 from this? Need to notify CS.
anna: Initial affected tenants: tenant-123 (SaaSCo), tenant-87 (FinanceApp), tenant-401 (Marketplace). Short-term impact: increased latency and 504s for ~2% of their requests during 1846805000-1846805400 window. We're pulling request ids for exact counts.
kevin: Paging note: I escalated to oncall-sre for backup. Also setting an emergency rule to explicit pin for known dedicated customers to avoid accidental spillover:

```
redwoodctl tenant pin --tenant tenant-123 --pool dedicated-west --duration 4h --reason="post-incident isolation"
```

sre-lead: Good. Also push a temporary guard in matcher to prefer explicit tenant_tag over regional fallback. Jordan/Anna to put a short patch to config repo and roll canary.
jordan: Prepared patch, creating canary. Snippet of problematic matcher fragment:

```
- match:
    selector: "pool:deds || selector:region:west"
    priority: 20
    action: route_to: dedicated
```

We need explicit tenant->dedicated first, then fallback by region. Current PR flips order in some conditions.
kevin: Observability update: dedicated-west errorrate back to baseline 0.3% at 1846806280. CPU on dedicated nodes normalized. Hosted latency returned to expected percentiles.
liaison-cs: Preparing short customer notifications for tenant-123 and tenant-87. Draft: "We briefly misrouted a portion of your traffic through a dedicated pool causing intermittent errors. Issue mitigated and we pinned your tenant while we follow up. Apologies — will send RCA." Want approval before send.
sre-lead: Approve draft. Add that we will share timeline and steps in follow-up.
anna: For postmortem notes: root cause = matcher rule ordering + a gap in preflight tests for combined region+tenant selectors. Remediation: 1) add unit test for matcher precedence, 2) canary policy rollout gating on 'spillover metrics', 3) create alert for 'spilled-hosted-to-dedicated' count > 10/min.
kevin: Confirming no further customer-facing impact. Marking incident as triaged. Will hand off to infra-ops for follow-ups and to CS for notifications.
customer-notify-bot: Scheduled message to tenant-123 & tenant-87 queued — template: "Incident 1846805123: brief routing misroute, mitigated. RCA forthcoming." ETA send 10m.
infra-ops: Follow-ups tracked: create change to matcher precedence, expand canary checks, add metric alert, schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
sre-lead: Thanks team. Handoff note: on-call returns to normal rotation. Filing incident ticket INC-2026-1846805123 and assigning owners: Jordan (root cause), Anna (forensics/data), Kevin (mitigation playbook), Liaison-cs (customer comms).
